answer.rationale: Finance mandates an 18% cost cut and the incumbent refuses to reopen price; the low-cost vendor quote alone meets the mandate. memory_c2 (day 38) confirms that moving primary supply to this same low-cost vendor cut unit cost sharply last year, onboarding was quick, and invoicing stayed accurate — reducing migration risk. memory_c6 (day 65) shows multi-year commitments unlock further volume pricing, which I would layer in after switching primary. Renewing with the incumbent fails the cost mandate; deferring risks the 14-day expiry with no auto-renew and 94% utilization leaves no buffer; adding a second source is incremental but doesn't address the mandated cut on its own and exceeds this cycle's single-decision capacity. Switching primary to the low-cost vendor directly satisfies the cost mandate while leaning on the strongest prior evidence for execution reliability.
